purpose: Bounded impasse check, not another generic research pass
product: 100 g sealed Japanese steamed/rolled/dried plain Camellia sinensis sencha, paid personal post; ordinary customs/arrival declarations allowed, no special permits/certificates/agency registration or advance approval
finding: No concrete safe untried public-source lead or overlooked general operative rule was identified. The same operative-text, specification-access or genuine scope-conflict barriers remain. This does not prove no qualifying exemption exists. Further identical generic searches or access retries would not supply a new basis for decision.
interpretationGuardrails: An applicable general processing rule or complete commodity list can resolve a route without naming tea and without a bespoke authority ruling.
Admissibility, inspection, registration relief, fee relief and certificate relief were kept distinct from any separate permit duty.
No missing online record was treated as absence of an operative specification, permission, or prohibition.
No status was changed because research was exhausted.

countries.externalEvidenceRequired: An applicable current processing/risk exemption under Law 7/2025 Article 5(5)(c), or published criteria placing this sencha outside the manufactured-product risk definition; receiving-emirate personal-food category if not already covered by a general allowance.
countries.whyPriorSourcesDoNotSettle: The law provides a certificate default and a power to make exceptions. JETRO specifically identifies a possible dried-tea exemption but does not confirm it under the January 2026 law. Personal-food registration relief is separate. Broad dead-plant language cannot erase the specific processing issue.
countries.impasseCheck: Current-law direct retrieval returned 403; exact JETRO route and current MOCCAE service already reviewed. No new operative list or untried public link identified.

countries.externalEvidenceRequired: The published allowed/prohibited commodity or processing lists required by 2019 regulation 5(1)(6)–(7), sufficient to apply 2017 Act 3(7) to manufactured sencha; full Gazette 1472 food-law text would resolve the separate private-food scope question.
countries.whyPriorSourcesDoNotSettle: The primary definition is risk-qualified. Act 11 is discretionary relief, while regulation 22(2) enumerates decorative plants/flowers and fruit. Neither is an automatic all-personal-food waiver. The processed-wood exception cannot extend to tea.
countries.impasseCheck: MAIL directory, actual 2017 Act, 2019 regulation, 2026 Dutch NPPO sheet and exact 2025 Gazette lead have been checked. No accessible operative list or new Gazette link identified.

countries.externalEvidenceRequired: A published Article 15(3) processing/category waiver or local criteria that establish whether this finished tea is a regulated manufactured plant product.
countries.whyPriorSourcesDoNotSettle: The complete NPPO-submitted law defines manufactured products by risk and authorises waivers; it does not grant a general processing waiver. Its annex lists pests, not an exhaustive commodity list. Article 24 concerns travellers. The personal-food undertaking remains routine, not a certificate blocker.
countries.impasseCheck: Complete 23-page law/annex and current services read. The MAFF processing footnote is conditional. No untried operative source link identified.

countries.externalEvidenceRequired: The meaning of PP 29 dried herbs as applied to Camellia sencha, or another general specification resolving its overlap with PP 23 dried plant material.
countries.whyPriorSourcesDoNotSettle: The current-linked January 2021 table has a real affirmative no-permit/no-certificate herb category. That narrower exemption must prevail if applicable. The table does not define herbs; applying PP 23 automatically is equally unsupported. Food regulation 18 may cover personal post and is not held open merely because it omits the word post.
countries.impasseCheck: Complete 2020 and 2021 tables, current ministry pages, ports guidance and 2014 food regulations reviewed. No further classification rule or concrete untried link identified.

countries.externalEvidenceRequired: A published criterion or supported local interpretation of the minor-processing boundary in 8 GAR 10100(g), sufficient to classify steamed/rolled/dried sencha.
countries.whyPriorSourcesDoNotSettle: Section 10120 allows dried human food, and 10102 does not list manufactured dried tea for a certificate. Section 10103 separately controls permits for plant products. The minor-processing definition may exclude finished tea, but the admissibility clause does not itself settle that boundary or waive permits.
countries.impasseCheck: Full official chapter, 2026 noncommercial-post permit form and current species guide reviewed; the corn-borer processing exception is commodity-specific. No new general processing source identified.

countries.externalEvidenceRequired: An applicable legal interpretation/general processing rule for the biological-nature definition, or an existing import-licence exemption covering this product.
countries.whyPriorSourcesDoNotSettle: Article 9(1) expressly supplies a postal certificate concession for certain non-agricultural-purpose materials. It does not waive the separate Article 7 licence; Article 9(2) expressly waives licences for seed samples only. Treating drink preparation as non-agricultural use does not close the licence issue.
countries.impasseCheck: Complete consolidated 2012/2020 law already read. COSQC source links returned 404 and do not establish private-post scope. No concrete untried operative exemption/list identified.

countries.externalEvidenceRequired: The current ministerial covered/exempt commodity decision under 2021 Instructions 3/8, including a complete list or general processing category applicable to sencha; ordinary personal-food clearance conditions if independently necessary.
countries.whyPriorSourcesDoNotSettle: The instructions depend on designations outside their text. A complete list could resolve tea by inclusion or omission, but the tariff code and zero duty are not that list. The 2026 medicinal-parcel consultation cannot cover ordinary sencha.
countries.impasseCheck: MOA/JFDA/Customs and the actual tariff/trade-portal paths checked. Ministry and official law-index retrieval returned 451. No new operative designation link identified.

countries.externalEvidenceRequired: The existing Biosecurity Act 26 import specification, including any compatible pre 2011 notice saved by 107, from the statutory public register or an authentic published copy.
countries.whyPriorSourcesDoNotSettle: Manufactured plant products are unconditionally within scope, but 25–26 make permit/certificate duties specification-dependent. A written application under 27 is mandatory only if no specification exists. An office-based register means online absence cannot establish that trigger. Food-law 10 kg relief does not waive biosecurity.
countries.impasseCheck: 2011 Act, 1976 predecessor, saved-rule clause, food regulations, newer ministry site and national FAO submission reviewed. No untried specification source identified.

countries.externalEvidenceRequired: An operative general classification or permit exception differentiating finished manufactured food from the plant/product class in 85-60.2-204.
countries.whyPriorSourcesDoNotSettle: Section 238 admits dried foods and 202 does not itself impose a tea certificate. Section 204 can separately require permits;108 shows admission can coexist with permits. Section 010 defines manufactured plant material, but 204 uses a different term. The traveller FAQ does not settle a postal permit classification.
countries.impasseCheck: Full code including 010, 108, 201–204, 238 and 501 plus current Finance guidance reviewed. No overlooked complete commodity list or concrete untried source identified.

countries.externalEvidenceRequired: A corroborated applicable processing/category rule under the 2011 Act and December 2025 notice, potentially the Agriculture Online System commodity conditions, or authenticated current text showing the older dried/packed-food distinction remains operative.
countries.whyPriorSourcesDoNotSettle: The current MFDA personal processed-food standard is favourable and is not held open for a tea-specific food form. It does not waive agriculture. The older English quarantine regulation cannot alone establish the effect of the later Act/current notice; provisional Dhivehi Act reading did not resolve that relationship.
countries.impasseCheck: 2011 Act IPPC upload, older English regulation, WTO identified portal and current MFDA standard reviewed. Act direct PDF 403; screenshots failed; agriculture portal redirects to login. No new public route identified.

countries.externalEvidenceRequired: The applicable current plant-product commodity/processing condition for Japan-origin sencha; a readable Food Safety Regulation 2/2010 Article 30/private-parcel scope if a separate food licence is relied on.
countries.whyPriorSourcesDoNotSettle: The plant-product definition is risk-qualified. Decision 32/2006 Article 34 postal concession waives fees only; Article 12 certificate relief concerns accompanied travellers. Decision 69/2024 waives personal-food registration but not every agricultural requirement. Old Australian tea conditions do not establish the Japan route.
countries.impasseCheck: Complete 2006 text and known alternatives checked; commodity lookup requiresCAPTCHA;2010 original food PDF repeatedly 403. No bypass or new operative source identified.

countries.externalEvidenceRequired: Current Order 324 CM of 16 March 2026 Annex 5, including its general processed-food categories and any tea conditions.
countries.whyPriorSourcesDoNotSettle: The current authority says this order replaced 740 CM. The reform summary does not provide the operative conditions; the old processed-food page cites the repealed order. The missing source is specific, and a general Annex 5 exemption could suffice without tea naming.
countries.impasseCheck: Both Lexpol hosts, short/exact queries, browser and direct retrieval, DBS index/media and government publication routes tried. Repeated timeouts, DNS/503 failures; no new public route identified.

countries.externalEvidenceRequired: Current enacted biosecurity framework and the operative processed-food/tea import condition or general exemption applying to personal postal consignments.
countries.whyPriorSourcesDoNotSettle: Government confirms 2025 bill passage and now namesPNGBA, but the current trade-office page links 1997 material and has inconsistent summaries. The 2017 draft is not enacted proof. Food Sanitation Act 30 notification concerns sale/business and cannot independently exclude the private recipient.
countries.impasseCheck: NPPO, Customs, MAFF, MICOR, Prime Minister and current trade-office/download links reviewed. No actual current commodity schedule or new enacted-law link identified.

countries.externalEvidenceRequired: An applicable published risk-based exception under Law 24/2005 Article 2, or processing/category criteria sufficient to decide sencha under Decision 61/2007 Article 1(8).
countries.whyPriorSourcesDoNotSettle: The complete implementing text covers post and requires permission/certificates for covered goods. Article 11 is traveller-only; Article 12 is diplomatic/research/public-body relief. The separate general personal-food document waiver does not decide plant-quarantine scope.
countries.impasseCheck: All 19 implementing articles recovered and read; current Act and personal-food guide checked. No further operative exemption/list lead identified.

countries.externalEvidenceRequired: The existing Director assessment or published general commodity condition under regulation 26 for manufactured plant material, including a sufficient processing exemption/category.
countries.whyPriorSourcesDoNotSettle: Regulation 26 expressly makes the permit duty depend on assessed serious exotic-pest risk. Regulations 23–25 concern fruit/vegetables and dried flowers and cannot automatically include tea. The separate food Act commercial scope is not a private-import permit duty.
countries.impasseCheck: Full Act/regulations and current origin-limited MPI/MICOR conditions reviewed. No current Japan-applicable assessment/list or concrete untried public link identified.

countries.externalEvidenceRequired: An operative interpretation/definition reconciling manufactured plant products with the specific bulk/loose-tea category, or the underlying 1993 rule/amendments with sufficient processing criteria.
countries.whyPriorSourcesDoNotSettle: The mail rule both limits product scope to non-manufactured goods and expressly waives only the permit for tea in bulk. Retail sealing alone does not resolve whether loose-leaf sencha is in that category. Neither ignoring the specific tea clause nor converting its permit waiver into a certificate waiver is defensible.
countries.impasseCheck: Current AIP reproduction, passenger materials and exact 1993/1996/1997 rule leads reviewed. The AIP page amendment is 2014. No new underlying text or general postal processing exemption identified.
